result.title: MoEDDI: Semantic Mixtures of Experts for Long Tailed Drug Drug Interaction Prediction
result.summary: Descriptor-based drug--drug interaction (DDI) models typically apply a single global predictor despite heterogeneous physicochemical evidence and severely long-tailed labels. We introduce \textbf{MoEDDI (Mixture-of-Experts for Drug--Drug Interaction prediction)}, a chemically organized mixture-of-experts that routes overlapping descriptor families using low-dimensional statistics and combines their sparse top-$2$ mixture with a global T-DDI pathway through a residual logit correction. The residual parameterization can exactly preserve a supplied T-DDI checkpoint at initialization, although the evaluated models are trained from scratch. Across complete test partitions with 178, 86, and 92 classes, MoEDDI improves macro-F1 over reproduced seed-2026 T-DDI baselines from 0.8284 to 0.8485, 0.4729 to 0.6536, and 0.1807 to 0.4671. On the 3,780-feature corpus, the lowest-support group (89 classes with fewer than 50 test examples) shows the largest mean classwise gain (+3.30 F1 points). Calibration improves on one corpus but worsens on two. These single-seed results support semantic conditional specialization while motivating matched ablations and distribution-shift evaluation.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 MoEDDI，用化学组织化的混合专家模型做长尾药物相互作用预测：以低维统计量为重叠的描述符家族做路由，稀疏 top-2 专家混合再经残差 logit 修正与全局 T-DDI 通路融合，在三个大规模类别划分上提升 macro-F1。
AI.relevance_reason: 与视觉推理主线无直接关系，但其稀疏条件路由与「残差保留基模型」的参数化，或可为 LVR 中动态计算分配、以及在叠加 latent 分支时保持原有视觉通路行为提供可供核查的线索。
